rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the most informative first experiment is to establish the simplest possible baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the minimal configuration in the search space: it uses the most standard RNA encoder (PCA), the simplest profile setting, and no image or fusion complexity. This gives a clean reference point for RNA-only performance. Knowing this floor is essential before testing whether (a) a better RNA encoder (scvi, scgpt) helps, (b) image modality adds value, (c) multiprofile aggregation improves things, or (d) multimodal fusion is worthwhile. Starting from the simplest baseline ensures that any subsequent gains can be attributed to specific design choices rather than confounded by multiple simultaneous changes. With 9 experiments remaining, this single baseline anchors the entire comparison hierarchy.

The only completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) yielded ~48.5% accuracy, a very weak baseline that provides little guidance on which design axis matters most. The highest-uncertainty, highest-impact question is whether the image modality carries useful predictive signal at all. config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the cleanest comparison to config_001: identical profile setting (singleprofile), same level of simplicity (no aggregation, no fusion), with only the modality swapped. If image-only substantially outperforms RNA-only, multimodal fusion (configs 16-51) becomes the primary direction; if it performs similarly poorly, I should focus on better single-modal representations (e.g., scgpt, scvi) rather than adding complexity. With 8 experiments remaining, establishing the per-modality ceiling before investing in fusion or encoder comparisons is the most information-efficient next step.

Evidence: config_001 (RNA-only, PCA n2000, single profile) achieves 48.5% accuracy, while config_010 (image-only, ResNet50) is very weak at 20.8%, establishing RNA as the dominant modality and suggesting the current best is RNA-based. The largest remaining uncertainty is whether the RNA representation itself can be substantially improved by switching from a linear PCA projection to a pretrained transformer encoder (scGPT). This experiment (config_007) isolates the encoder effect by keeping profile_setting=singleprofile and model_setting=rna_only identical to config_001, changing only the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scGPT. If scGPT yields a meaningful gain, it redefines the RNA baseline and informs all downstream multimodal experiments; if it does not, PCA is confirmed as sufficient and remaining budget can focus on profile/aggregation/fusion dimensions. With 7 experiments left, resolving the encoder question early is the highest-value single-variable test before committing to more complex multimodal or multiprofile configurations.

Evidence: config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the clear best at 0.485 acc, while scgpt (0.411) and image-only resnet50 (0.208) are substantially weaker. All three completed experiments used singleprofile, so the effect of multiprofile is completely unexplored. Question: Does moving from singleprofile to multiprofile with the best-performing RNA encoder (pca_n2000) improve accuracy? config_002 tests this with the simplest aggregation (avgpool), isolating the profile-setting effect without introducing additional complexity (transformer). This is the best use of experiment 4 because it directly extends our strongest result along one axis, and the answer will inform whether to invest remaining budget in multiprofile variants (transformer, multimodal) or focus on other dimensions like image encoder quality or fusion strategy.

Evidence: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) achieved the best accuracy so far (0.591), a substantial +10.6% gain over singleprofile PCA (config_001, 0.485), confirming that multiprofile aggregation is the most impactful design axis. RNA dominates over image (0.485 vs 0.208). Question: Does transformer aggregation outperform simple avgpool for aggregating multiple PCA profiles? This is a clean single-variable comparison (only aggregation changes from config_002). Rationale: With 5 experiments remaining, exploiting the strongest direction while isolating the aggregation effect is the highest-information next step. If transformer wins, it directly informs the best aggregation choice for later multimodal experiments; if it ties or loses, avgpool is confirmed as sufficient and we can shift budget toward testing scvi or multimodal fusion.

Evidence: The current best is config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) at 0.591 accuracy. We know multiprofile+avgpool is a strong combination (+10.6 pts over singleprofile), and avgpool beats transformer. In singleprofile, pca_n2000 (0.485) outperforms scgpt (0.411), but scvi_n200 has not yet been tested in any setting. Question: Does scvi_n200, a learned latent-space encoder, improve on pca_n2000 in the multiprofile+avgpool setting where we've already seen the largest gains? This is a single-variable swap (encoder only) from our best config, cleanly isolating the representation effect. Why this is the best use of experiment 6: With 4 experiments remaining, we need to determine whether a better RNA encoder exists before committing budget to multimodal fusion (which currently rests on a very weak image signal at 0.208). If scvi_n200 improves on 0.591, it reshapes the multimodal strategy; if not, we confirm pca_n2000 as optimal and can pivot remaining experiments to testing whether multimodal fusion or a stronger image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) adds value on top of the best RNA baseline.

Evidence: config_005 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) is the current best at 0.650 acc. For pca_n2000, avgpool (0.591) clearly outperformed transformer (0.519), but scvi_n200 produces a fundamentally different, learned low-dimensional representation that may interact differently with attention-based aggregation. This experiment tests the single variable of aggregation (avgpool→transformer) while holding the best encoder and profile setting fixed, directly extending the current best config. It is the cleanest next step: if transformer wins, we find a new best RNA-only config; if not, we confirm avgpool is optimal for scvi_n200 and can dedicate the remaining 3 experiments to the higher-risk/higher-reward multimodal space (e.g., scvi_n200 + ViT-L fusion). Changing only one variable avoids confounding and gives clear attribution.

Evidence: RNA-only models dominate (best: scvi_n200/multiprofile/transformer at 0.653), while image-only with resnet50 is very weak (0.208). The largest unexplored design axis is whether multimodal fusion can complement the strong RNA signal with any useful image information. This experiment (config_032) pairs the best RNA configuration (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer aggregation) with resnet50 image features via simple concat fusion, isolating the effect of adding the image modality to the already-optimal RNA pipeline. Using resnet50 (rather than untested ViT-L) keeps the image encoder fixed to a known quantity, so any performance change can be attributed to fusion rather than encoder quality. If concat fusion improves on 0.653, the final experiment can test weighted fusion or a stronger image encoder; if it degrades, we confirm that the weak image signal is not complementary and the RNA-only result stands as the best within budget.

The current best is config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) at 0.688 accuracy. The image-only resnet50 was very weak (0.208), suggesting the image modality contributes limited signal, yet multimodal fusion still yielded a ~3.5% gain over RNA-only (0.653). This raises the question of whether the fusion method is optimal: concat treats both modalities equally, while weighted fusion could learn to downweight the weaker image stream. Config_033 changes only the fusion method (concat → weighted) from the current best, isolating this single variable. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, a minimal-risk, targeted exploitation of the best-known configuration is the safest path to a potential small improvement, and it provides a clean comparison to confirm or reject whether fusion strategy matters in this regime.

The best result so far is config_033 (0.7131 acc) using multimodal/multiprofile/scVI_n200/ResNet50/transformer/weighted. The image modality adds ~6% over the best RNA-only model (0.6530), yet ResNet50 alone scored only 0.2079, suggesting the image encoder's representational quality is a bottleneck. Config_039 makes a single clean change—swapping ResNet50 for the stronger imagenet_vit_l—while keeping all other validated-optimal settings (scVI_n200, multiprofile, transformer, weighted fusion). This directly tests whether a more powerful image encoder can push the multimodal model beyond 0.7131. As the final experiment, exploiting the strongest identified direction with the highest-potential single upgrade is the best use of the last budget slot.
